# xh

xh is a command-line HTTP client for sending and inspecting HTTP requests. It provides a friendly, concise interface for making HTTP requests and examining responses.

Usage

  xh [OPTIONS] <[METHOD] URL> [REQUEST_ITEM]...

Examples

  # Send a GET request
  xh http://example.org/json

  # Send a POST request with JSON-like key/value items
  xh http://example.org/post name=alice age:=30

  # Read the request body from stdin
  echo "[1,2,3]" | xh post http://example.org/post

Installation

Prebuilt binaries are available on the project's releases page:
https://github.com/ducaale/xh/releases

Alternatively, install using your system's package manager if available (e.g. Homebrew, apt, pacman, etc.).

For more detailed usage run:

  xh help

---
# xh
[![Version info](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/xh.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/xh)
[![Packaging status](https://repology.org/badge/tiny-repos/xh.svg)](https://repology.org/project/xh/versions)

`xh` is a friendly and fast tool for sending HTTP requests. It reimplements as much
as possible of [HTTPie's](https://httpie.io/) excellent design, with a focus
on improved performance.

[![asciicast](/assets/xh-demo.gif)](https://asciinema.org/a/475190)

Run `xh help` for more detailed information.

### Request Items

`xh` uses [HTTPie's request-item syntax](https://httpie.io/docs/cli/request-items) to set headers, request body, query string, etc.

- `=`/`:=` for setting the request body's JSON or form fields (`=` for strings and `:=` for other JSON types).
- `==` for adding query strings.
- `@` for including files in multipart requests e.g `picture@hello.jpg` or `picture@hello.jpg;type=image/jpeg;filename=goodbye.jpg`.
- `:` for adding or removing headers e.g `connection:keep-alive` or `connection:`.
- `;` for including headers with empty values e.g `header-without-value;`.

An `@` prefix can be used to read a value from a file. For example: `x-api-key:@api-key.txt`.

The request body can also be read from standard input, or from a file using `@filename`.

To construct a complex JSON object, a JSON path can be used as a key e.g `app[container][0][id]=090-5`.
For more information on this syntax, refer to https://httpie.io/docs/cli/nested-json.

### Shorthand form for URLs

Similar to HTTPie, specifying the scheme portion of the request URL is optional, and a leading colon works as shorthand
for localhost. `:8000` is equivalent to `localhost:8000`, and `:/path` is equivalent to `localhost/path`.

`http://httpbin.org/json` becomes `http ://httpbin.org/json`.


```sh

xh localhost:3000/users        # resolves to http://localhost:3000/users
xh :3000/users                 # resolves to http://localhost:3000/users
xh :/users                     # resolves to http://localhost:80/users
xh example.com                 # resolves to http://example.com
xh ://example.com              # resolves to http://example.com

`xh` will default to HTTPS scheme if the binary name is one of `xhs`, `https`, or `xhttps`. If you have installed `xh`
via a package manager, both `xh` and `xhs` should be available by default. Otherwise, you need to create one like this:

```sh

.TH XH 1 2025-12-16 0.25.2 "User Commands"

.SH NAME
xh \- Friendly and fast tool for sending HTTP requests

.SH SYNOPSIS
.B xh
[\fIOPTIONS\fR]
[\fIMETHOD\fR]
\fIURL\fR
[\-\-\]
[\fIREQUEST_ITEM\fR ...]

.SH DESCRIPTION

\fBxh\fR is an HTTP client with a friendly command line interface. It strives to
have readable output and easy-to-use options.

xh is mostly compatible with HTTPie: see \fBhttp\fR(1).

The \fB--curl\fR option can be used to print a \fBcurl\fR(1) translation of the
command instead of sending a request.

.SH POSITIONAL ARGUMENTS
.TP 4
[\fIMETHOD\fR]\fI
The HTTP method to use for the request.

This defaults to GET, or to POST if the request contains a body.
.TP
\fIURL\fR
The URL to request.

The URL scheme defaults to "http://" normally, or "https://" if
the program is invoked as "xhs".

A leading colon works as shorthand for localhost. ":8000" is equivalent
to "localhost:8000", and ":/path" is equivalent to "localhost/path".
.TP
[\fIREQUEST_ITEM\fR ...]
Optional key\-value pairs to be included in the request.

The separator is used to determine the type:
.RS 8
.TP 4
key==value
Add a query string to the URL.
.TP 4
key=value
Add a JSON property (\-\-json) or form field (\-\-form) to the request body.
.TP 4
key:=value
Add a field with a literal JSON value to the request body.

Example: "numbers:=[1,2,3] enabled:=true"
.TP 4
key@filename
Upload a file (requires \-\-form or \-\-multipart).

To set the filename and mimetype, ";type=" and ";filename=" can be used respectively.

Example: "pfp@ra.jpg;type=image/jpeg;filename=profile.jpg"
.TP 4
@filename
Use a file as the request body.
.TP 4
header:value
Add a header, e.g. "user\-agent:foobar"
.TP 4
header:
Unset a header, e.g. "connection:"
.TP 4
header;
Add a header with an empty value.
.RE

.RS
An "@" prefix can be used to read a value from a file. For example: "x\-api\-key:@api\-key.txt".

A backslash can be used to escape special characters, e.g. "weird\\:key=value".

To construct a complex JSON object, the REQUEST_ITEM's key can be set to a JSON path instead of a field name. For more information on this syntax, refer to https://httpie.io/docs/cli/nested\-json.
.RE

.SH OPTIONS
Each --OPTION can be reset with a --no-OPTION argument.
.TP 4
\fB\-j\fR, \fB\-\-json\fR
(default) Serialize data items from the command line as a JSON object.

Overrides both \-\-form and \-\-multipart.
.TP 4
\fB\-f\fR, \fB\-\-form\fR
Serialize data items from the command line as form fields.

Overrides both \-\-json and \-\-multipart.
.TP 4
\fB\-\-multipart\fR
Like \-\-form, but force a multipart/form\-data request even without files.

Overrides both \-\-json and \-\-form.
.TP 4
\fB\-\-raw\fR=\fIRAW\fR
Pass raw request data without extra processing.
.TP 4
\fB\-\-pretty\fR=\fISTYLE\fR
Controls output processing. Possible values are:

    all      (default) Enable both coloring and formatting
    colors   Apply syntax highlighting to output
    format   Pretty\-print json and sort headers
    none     Disable both coloring and formatting

Defaults to "format" if the NO_COLOR env is set and to "none" if stdout is not tty.
.TP 4
\fB\-\-format\-options\fR=\fIFORMAT_OPTIONS\fR
Set output formatting options. Supported option are:

    json.indent:<NUM>
    json.format:<true|false>
    headers.sort:<true|false>

Example: \-\-format\-options=json.indent:2,headers.sort:false.
.TP 4
\fB\-s\fR, \fB\-\-style\fR=\fITHEME\fR
Output coloring style.

[possible values: auto, solarized, monokai, fruity]
.TP 4
\fB\-\-response\-charset\fR=\fIENCODING\fR
Override the response encoding for terminal display purposes.

Example: \-\-response\-charset=latin1.
.TP 4
\fB\-\-response\-mime\fR=\fIMIME_TYPE\fR
Override the response mime type for coloring and formatting for the terminal.

Example: \-\-response\-mime=application/json.
.TP 4
\fB\-p\fR, \fB\-\-print\fR=\fIFORMAT\fR
String specifying what the output should contain

    'H' request headers
    'B' request body
    'h' response headers
    'b' response body
    'm' response metadata

Example: \-\-print=Hb.
.TP 4
\fB\-h\fR, \fB\-\-headers\fR
Print only the response headers. Shortcut for \-\-print=h.
.TP 4
\fB\-b\fR, \fB\-\-body\fR
Print only the response body. Shortcut for \-\-print=b.
.TP 4
\fB\-m\fR, \fB\-\-meta\fR
Print only the response metadata. Shortcut for \-\-print=m.
.TP 4
\fB\-v\fR, \fB\-\-verbose\fR
Print the whole request as well as the response.

Additionally, this enables \-\-all for printing intermediary requests/responses while following redirects.

Using verbose twice i.e. \-vv will print the response metadata as well.

Equivalent to \-\-print=HhBb \-\-all.
.TP 4
\fB\-\-debug\fR
Print full error stack traces and debug log messages.

Logging can be configured in more detail using the `$RUST_LOG` environment variable. Set `RUST_LOG=trace` to show even more messages. See https://docs.rs/env_logger/0.11.3/env_logger/#enabling\-logging.
.TP 4
\fB\-\-all\fR
Show any intermediary requests/responses while following redirects with \-\-follow.
.TP 4
\fB\-P\fR, \fB\-\-history\-print\fR=\fIFORMAT\fR
The same as \-\-print but applies only to intermediary requests/responses.
.TP 4
\fB\-q\fR, \fB\-\-quiet\fR
Do not print to stdout or stderr.

Using quiet twice i.e. \-qq will suppress warnings as well.
.TP 4
\fB\-S\fR, \fB\-\-stream\fR
Always stream the response body.
.TP 4
\fB\-x\fR, \fB\-\-compress\fR
Content compressed (encoded) with Deflate algorithm.

The Content\-Encoding header is set to deflate.

Compression is skipped if it appears that compression ratio is negative. Compression can be forced by repeating this option.

Note: Compression cannot be used if the Content\-Encoding request header is present.
.TP 4
\fB\-o\fR, \fB\-\-output\fR=\fIFILE\fR
Save output to FILE instead of stdout.
.TP 4
\fB\-d\fR, \fB\-\-download\fR
</output>

          Optional key-value pairs to be included in the request.

          "x-api-key:@api-key.txt".

.TH XH 1 2026-04-29 0.25.3 "User Commands"

.SH NAME
xh \- Friendly and fast tool for sending HTTP requests

.SH SYNOPSIS
.B xh
[\fIOPTIONS\fR]
[\fIMETHOD\fR]
\fIURL\fR
[\-\-\]
[\fIREQUEST_ITEM\fR ...]

.SH DESCRIPTION

\fBxh\fR is an HTTP client with a friendly command line interface. It strives to
have readable output and easy-to-use options.

xh is mostly compatible with HTTPie: see \fBhttp\fR(1).

The \fB--curl\fR option can be used to print a \fBcurl\fR(1) translation of the
command instead of sending a request.

.SH POSITIONAL ARGUMENTS
.TP 4
[\fIMETHOD\fR]\fI
The HTTP method to use for the request.

This defaults to GET, or to POST if the request contains a body.
.TP
\fIURL\fR
The URL to request.

The URL scheme defaults to "http://" normally, or "https://" if
the program is invoked as "xhs".

A leading colon works as shorthand for localhost. ":8000" is equivalent
to "localhost:8000", and ":/path" is equivalent to "localhost/path".
.TP
[\fIREQUEST_ITEM\fR ...]
Optional key\-value pairs to be included in the request.

The separator is used to determine the type:
.RS 8
.TP 4
key==value
Add a query string to the URL.
.TP 4
key=value
Add a JSON property (\-\-json) or form field (\-\-form) to the request body.
</output>

        self.send_header('Content-Length', len(content))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(content)

t = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever)

def get_theme(name):
    """Get theme by name, defaulting to auto."""
    return THEMES.get(name, THEMES["auto"])


def colorize_request_line(method, path, http_ver, theme):
    """Colorize an HTTP request line."""
    t = get_theme(theme)
    r = t["reset"]
    return (
        f"{r}{t['method']}{method}{r} "
        f"{r}{t['url']}{path}{r} "
        f"{r}{t['http_kw']}HTTP{r}/{r}{t['version']}{http_ver}{r}"
    )


def colorize_response_line(http_ver, status_code, status_text, theme):
    """Colorize an HTTP response status line."""
    t = get_theme(theme)
    r = t["reset"]
    return (
        f"{r}{t['http_kw']}HTTP{r}/{r}{t['version']}{http_ver}{r} "
        f"{r}{t['status_code']}{status_code}{r} "
        f"{r}{t['status_text']}{status_text}{r}"
    )

    t = get_theme(theme)
    r = t["reset"]

    return (

        f"{r}{t['header_value']}{value}{r}{nl}"
    )

                string_start = i

                        i += 1

    """Parse a single request item and return (key, separator, value)."""
    # Check for escape sequences
    # The separators in order of priority: :=, ==, =, @, :, ;
    
    # We need to handle backslash escapes
    # A backslash before a separator character escapes it
    
    # Find the first unescaped separator
    i = 0
    while i < len(item):
        if item[i] == '\\' and i + 1 < len(item):
            i += 2
            continue
        
        # Check for two-char separators first
        if i + 1 < len(item):
            two = item[i:i+2]
            if two == ':=':
                key = unescape(item[:i])
                value = item[i+2:]
                return key, ':=', value
            elif two == '==':
                key = unescape(item[:i])
                value = item[i+2:]
                return key, '==', value
        
        # Check for one-char separators
        ch = item[i]
        if ch == '=':
            key = unescape(item[:i])
            value = item[i+1:]
            return key, '=', value
        elif ch == '@':
            key = unescape(item[:i])
            value = item[i+1:]
            return key, '@', value
        elif ch == ':':
            key = unescape(item[:i])
            value = item[i+1:]
            return key, ':', value
        elif ch == ';':
            key = unescape(item[:i])
            value = item[i+1:]
            return key, ';', value
        
        i += 1
    
    return item, None, None


def unescape(s):
    """Remove backslash escapes from a string."""
    result = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(s):
        if s[i] == '\\' and i + 1 < len(s):
            result.append(s[i+1])
            i += 2
        else:
            result.append(s[i])
            i += 1
    return ''.join(result)


def normalize_url(url, https=False, default_scheme='http'):
    """Normalize the URL, handling localhost shorthand."""
    # Handle :// prefix (strip leading //)
    if url.startswith('://'):
        url = url[3:]
    
    # Handle :port or :/path shorthand for localhost
    if url.startswith(':'):
        rest = url[1:]
        if rest.startswith('/'):
            # :/path -> localhost/path
            url = f'localhost{url}'
        else:
            # :8080 or :8080/path -> localhost:8080[/path]
            url = f'localhost{url}'
    
    # Add scheme if missing
    if '://' not in url:
        # Check if the name suggests HTTPS
        scheme = default_scheme
        if https:
            scheme = 'https'
        url = f'{scheme}://{url}'
    
    return url

    """Set a value in a nested dict/list using HTTPie's JSON path syntax."""
    # Parse the key path: app[container][0][id]
    parts = _parse_key_path(key)
    
    if len(parts) == 1:
        obj[parts[0]] = value
        return
    
    # Navigate/create the path
    current = obj
    for i, part in enumerate(parts[:-1]):
        next_part = parts[i + 1]
        
        if isinstance(current, dict):
            if part not in current:
                # Create next level
                if isinstance(next_part, int):
                    current[part] = []
                else:
                    current[part] = {}
            current = current[part]
        elif isinstance(current, list):
            while len(current) <= part:
                # Determine what to fill with
                if isinstance(next_part, int):
                    current.append([])
                else:
                    current.append({})
            current = current[part]
    
    last = parts[-1]
    if isinstance(current, dict):
        current[last] = value
    elif isinstance(current, list):
        while len(current) <= last:
            current.append(None)
        current[last] = value

    main = re.split(r'\[', key)
    
    if not main:

    parts.append(main[0])
    for part in main[1:]:
        part = part.rstrip(']')
        try:
            parts.append(int(part))

            parts.append(part)

    boundary = f"{uuid.uuid4().hex[:16]}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:16]}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:16]}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:16]}"
    
    parts = []
    
    for ptype, key, value in body_params:
        parts.append(
            f'--{boundary}\r\n'
            f'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="{key}"\r\n'
            f'\r\n'
            f'{value}\r\n'
        )
    
    for key, filepath, mime_type, filename in files:
        if filename is None:
            filename = os.path.basename(filepath)
        
        if mime_type is None:
            mime_type, _ = mimetypes.guess_type(filepath)
        
        try:
            with open(filepath, 'rb') as f:
                file_data = f.read()
        except (IOError, OSError) as e:
            sys.stderr.write(f"xh: error: cannot read file '{filepath}': {e}\n")
            sys.exit(1)
        
        cd_line = f'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="{key}"; filename="{filename}"\r\n'
        ct_line = ''
        if mime_type:
            ct_line = f'Content-Type: {mime_type}\r\n'
        
        part = f'--{boundary}\r\n{cd_line}{ct_line}\r\n'.encode()
        part += file_data
        part += b'\r\n'
        parts.append(part)
    
    # Final boundary
    body_parts = []
    for p in parts:
        if isinstance(p, str):
            body_parts.append(p.encode())
        else:
            body_parts.append(p)
    
    final = f'--{boundary}--\r\n'.encode()
    body_parts.append(final)
    
    body = b''.join(body_parts)
    content_type = f'multipart/form-data; boundary={boundary}'
    
    return body, content_type

                i += 4

            elif ch == '-' or ch.isdigit():
                # Number

                while j < len(text) and (text[j] in '-+.eE' or text[j].isdigit()):

                num = text[i:j]
                result.append(f"{t['json_number']}{num}{r}")
                i = j
                continue
            else:

def parse_item(item):
    """Parse a single request item and return (key, separator, value)."""
    # Check for escape sequences
    # The separators in order of priority: :=, ==, =, @, :, ;
    
    # We need to handle backslash escapes
    # A backslash before a separator character escapes it
    
    # Find the first unescaped separator
    i = 0
    while i < len(item):
        if item[i] == '\\' and i + 1 < len(item):
            i += 2
            continue
        
        # Check for two-char separators first
        if i + 1 < len(item):
            two = item[i:i+2]
            if two == ':=':
                key = unescape(item[:i])
                value = item[i+2:]
                return key, ':=', value
            elif two == '==':
                key = unescape(item[:i])
                value = item[i+2:]
                return key, '==', value
        
        # Check for one-char separators
        ch = item[i]
        if ch == '=':
            key = unescape(item[:i])
            value = item[i+1:]
            return key, '=', value
        elif ch == '@':
            key = unescape(item[:i])
            value = item[i+1:]
            return key, '@', value
        elif ch == ':':
            key = unescape(item[:i])
            value = item[i+1:]
            return key, ':', value
        elif ch == ';':
            key = unescape(item[:i])
            value = item[i+1:]
            return key, ';', value
        
        i += 1
    
    return item, None, None


def unescape(s):
    """Remove backslash escapes from a string."""
    result = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(s):
        if s[i] == '\\' and i + 1 < len(s):
            result.append(s[i+1])
            i += 2
        else:
            result.append(s[i])
            i += 1
    return ''.join(result)

    """Normalize the URL, handling localhost shorthand."""
    # Handle :// prefix (strip leading //)
    if url.startswith('://'):
        url = url[3:]
    
    # Handle :port or :/path shorthand for localhost
    if url.startswith(':'):
        rest = url[1:]
        if rest.startswith('/'):
            # :/path -> localhost/path
            url = f'localhost{url}'
        else:
            # :8080 or :8080/path -> localhost:8080[/path]
            url = f'localhost{url}'
    
    # Add scheme if missing
    if '://' not in url:
        # Check if the name suggests HTTPS
        scheme = default_scheme
        if https:
            scheme = 'https'
        url = f'{scheme}://{url}'
    
    return url

    parts = _parse_key_path(key)
    
    if len(parts) == 1:
        obj[parts[0]] = value
        return
    
    # Navigate/create the path
    current = obj
    for i, part in enumerate(parts[:-1]):
        next_part = parts[i + 1]
        
        if isinstance(current, dict):
            if part not in current:
                # Create next level
                if isinstance(next_part, int):
                    current[part] = []
                else:
                    current[part] = {}
            current = current[part]
        elif isinstance(current, list):
            while len(current) <= part:
                # Determine what to fill with
                if isinstance(next_part, int):
                    current.append([])
                else:
                    current.append({})
            current = current[part]
    
    last = parts[-1]
    if isinstance(current, dict):
        current[last] = value
    elif isinstance(current, list):
        while len(current) <= last:
            current.append(None)
        current[last] = value

    """Parse a JSON path key like 'app[container][0][id]' into ['app', 'container', 0, 'id']."""

    parts.append(main[0])
    for part in main[1:]:
        part = part.rstrip(']')

    parts = []

        parts.append(
            f'--{boundary}\r\n'
            f'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="{key}"\r\n'
            f'\r\n'
            f'{value}\r\n'
        )

        if filename is None:
            filename = os.path.basename(filepath)
        
        if mime_type is None:
            mime_type, _ = mimetypes.guess_type(filepath)
        
        try:

                file_data = f.read()
        except (IOError, OSError) as e:
            sys.stderr.write(f"xh: error: cannot read file '{filepath}': {e}\n")
            sys.exit(1)
        
        cd_line = f'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="{key}"; filename="{filename}"\r\n'
        ct_line = ''
        if mime_type:
            ct_line = f'Content-Type: {mime_type}\r\n'
        
        part = f'--{boundary}\r\n{cd_line}{ct_line}\r\n'.encode()
        part += file_data
        part += b'\r\n'
        parts.append(part)

    body_parts = []
    for p in parts:

    body_parts.append(final)
    
    body = b''.join(body_parts)
    content_type = f'multipart/form-data; boundary={boundary}'

def is_json_content_type(ct):

    if not ct:

def is_text_content_type(ct):
    """Check if content type is text."""
    if not ct:

def parse_request_items(items, is_form=False, is_multipart=False, is_json=True):

def parse_item(item):
    """Parse a single request item and return (key, separator, value)."""
    # Check for escape sequences
    # The separators in order of priority: :=, ==, =, @, :, ;
    
    # We need to handle backslash escapes
    # A backslash before a separator character escapes it
    
    # Find the first unescaped separator
    i = 0
    while i < len(item):
        if item[i] == '\\' and i + 1 < len(item):
            i += 2
            continue
        
        # Check for two-char separators first
        if i + 1 < len(item):
            two = item[i:i+2]
            if two == ':=':
                key = unescape(item[:i])
                value = item[i+2:]
                return key, ':=', value
            elif two == '==':
                key = unescape(item[:i])
                value = item[i+2:]
                return key, '==', value
        
        # Check for one-char separators
        ch = item[i]
        if ch == '=':
            key = unescape(item[:i])
            value = item[i+1:]
            return key, '=', value
        elif ch == '@':
            key = unescape(item[:i])
            value = item[i+1:]
            return key, '@', value
        elif ch == ':':
            key = unescape(item[:i])
            value = item[i+1:]
            return key, ':', value
        elif ch == ';':
            key = unescape(item[:i])
            value = item[i+1:]
            return key, ';', value
        
        i += 1
    
    return item, None, None


def unescape(s):
    """Remove backslash escapes from a string."""
    result = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(s):
        if s[i] == '\\' and i + 1 < len(s):
            result.append(s[i+1])
            i += 2
        else:
            result.append(s[i])
            i += 1
    return ''.join(result)

    """Normalize the URL, handling localhost shorthand."""
    # Handle :// prefix (strip leading //)
    if url.startswith('://'):
        url = url[3:]
    
    # Handle :port or :/path shorthand for localhost
    if url.startswith(':'):
        rest = url[1:]
        if rest.startswith('/'):
            # :/path -> localhost/path
            url = f'localhost{url}'
        else:
            # :8080 or :8080/path -> localhost:8080[/path]
            url = f'localhost{url}'
    
    # Add scheme if missing
    if '://' not in url:
        # Check if the name suggests HTTPS
        scheme = default_scheme
        if https:
            scheme = 'https'
        url = f'{scheme}://{url}'
    
    return url

    """Set a value in a nested dict/list using HTTPie's JSON path syntax."""
    # Parse the key path: app[container][0][id]
    parts = _parse_key_path(key)
    
    if len(parts) == 1:
        obj[parts[0]] = value
        return
    
    # Navigate/create the path
    current = obj
    for i, part in enumerate(parts[:-1]):
        next_part = parts[i + 1]
        
        if isinstance(current, dict):
            if part not in current:
                # Create next level
                if isinstance(next_part, int):
                    current[part] = []
                else:
                    current[part] = {}
            current = current[part]
        elif isinstance(current, list):
            while len(current) <= part:
                # Determine what to fill with
                if isinstance(next_part, int):
                    current.append([])
                else:
                    current.append({})
            current = current[part]
    
    last = parts[-1]
    if isinstance(current, dict):
        current[last] = value
    elif isinstance(current, list):
        while len(current) <= last:
            current.append(None)
        current[last] = value


def _parse_key_path(key):
    """Parse a JSON path key like 'app[container][0][id]' into ['app', 'container', 0, 'id']."""
    parts = []

    main = re.split(r'\[', key)
    
    if not main:
        return [key]
    
    parts.append(main[0])
    for part in main[1:]:
        part = part.rstrip(']')
        try:
            parts.append(int(part))
        except ValueError:
            parts.append(part)

def build_multipart_body(body_params, files):
    """Build a multipart/form-data body."""
    boundary = f"{uuid.uuid4().hex[:16]}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:16]}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:16]}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:16]}"
    
    parts = []
    
    for ptype, key, value in body_params:
        parts.append(
            f'--{boundary}\r\n'
            f'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="{key}"\r\n'
            f'\r\n'
            f'{value}\r\n'
        )
    
    for key, filepath, mime_type, filename in files:
        if filename is None:
            filename = os.path.basename(filepath)
        
        if mime_type is None:
            mime_type, _ = mimetypes.guess_type(filepath)
        
        try:
            with open(filepath, 'rb') as f:
                file_data = f.read()
        except (IOError, OSError) as e:
            sys.stderr.write(f"xh: error: cannot read file '{filepath}': {e}\n")
            sys.exit(1)
        
        cd_line = f'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="{key}"; filename="{filename}"\r\n'
        ct_line = ''
        if mime_type:
            ct_line = f'Content-Type: {mime_type}\r\n'
        
        part = f'--{boundary}\r\n{cd_line}{ct_line}\r\n'.encode()
        part += file_data
        part += b'\r\n'
        parts.append(part)
    
    # Final boundary
    body_parts = []
    for p in parts:
        if isinstance(p, str):
            body_parts.append(p.encode())
        else:
            body_parts.append(p)
    
    final = f'--{boundary}--\r\n'.encode()
    body_parts.append(final)
    
    body = b''.join(body_parts)
    content_type = f'multipart/form-data; boundary={boundary}'
    
    return body, content_type

            elif text[i:i+5] == 'false':
                result.append(f"{t['json_bool']}false{r}")
                i += 5
                continue
            elif text[i:i+4] == 'null':
                result.append(f"{t['json_null']}null{r}")
                i += 4
                continue
            elif ch == '-' or ch.isdigit():
                # Number
                j = i
                while j < len(text) and (text[j] in '-+.eE' or text[j].isdigit()):
                    j += 1
                num = text[i:j]
                result.append(f"{t['json_number']}{num}{r}")
                i = j
                continue
            else:
                result.append(ch)
        
        i += 1
    
    return ''.join(result)


def format_json(text, indent=4, sort_keys=False):
    """Parse and pretty-print JSON."""
    try:
        obj = json.loads(text)
        return json.dumps(obj, indent=indent, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=sort_keys)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError):
        return text


def is_json_content_type(ct):
    """Check if content type is JSON."""
    if not ct:
        return False
    ct = ct.lower().split(';')[0].strip()
    return ct in ('application/json', 'text/json') or '+json' in ct


def is_text_content_type(ct):
    """Check if content type is text."""
    if not ct:
        return False
    ct = ct.lower().split(';')[0].strip()
    return (ct.startswith('text/') or 
            ct in ('application/json', 'application/xml', 'application/javascript',
                   'application/x-www-form-urlencoded') or
            '+json' in ct or '+xml' in ct)


def parse_request_items(items, is_form=False, is_multipart=False, is_json=True):
    """Parse request items and return headers, body_params, query_params, files."""
    headers = []
    body_params = []
    query_params = []
    files = []
    body_file = None
    
    SEPARATORS = [':=', '==', '=', '@', ':', ';']
    
    for item in items:
        # Check for file body @filename
        if item.startswith('@') and not item.startswith('@{'):
            # Body from file
            filename = item[1:]
            body_file = filename
            continue
        
        # Parse the item
        key, sep, value = parse_item(item)
        
        if sep == '==':
            query_params.append((key, value))
        elif sep == '=':
            # JSON string or form field
            if value.startswith('@'):
                # Value from file
                filepath = value[1:]
                try:
                    with open(filepath, 'rb') as f:
                        file_value = f.read()
                    # Decode as UTF-8, strip trailing newlines for header values
                    try:
                        value = file_value.decode('utf-8')
                    except UnicodeDecodeError:
                        value = file_value.decode('latin-1')
                except (IOError, OSError) as e:
                    sys.stderr.write(f"xh: error: cannot read file '{filepath}': {e}\n")
                    sys.exit(1)
            body_params.append(('string', key, value))
        elif sep == ':=':
            # JSON literal value
            if value.startswith('@'):
                filepath = value[1:]
                try:
                    with open(filepath, 'r') as f:
                        value = f.read()
                except (IOError, OSError) as e:
                    sys.stderr.write(f"xh: error: cannot read file '{filepath}': {e}\n")
                    sys.exit(1)
            body_params.append(('json', key, value))
        elif sep == '@':
            # File upload for multipart
            # Format: key@filename[;type=mime][;filename=name]
            filepath = value
            mime_type = None
            filename = None
            
            # Parse ;type= and ;filename=
            parts = value.split(';')
            filepath = parts[0]
            for part in parts[1:]:
                if part.startswith('type='):
                    mime_type = part[5:]
                elif part.startswith('filename='):
                    filename = part[9:]
            
            files.append((key, filepath, mime_type, filename))
        elif sep == ':':
            # Header
            if value.startswith('@'):
                # Value from file
                filepath = value[1:]
                try:
                    with open(filepath, 'rb') as f:
                        file_value = f.read()
                    # Decode, strip trailing newline
                    try:
                        value = file_value.decode('utf-8').rstrip('\n').rstrip('\r')
                    except UnicodeDecodeError:
                        value = file_value.decode('latin-1').rstrip('\n').rstrip('\r')
                    # Check for embedded newlines (invalid header value)
                    if '\n' in value or '\r' in value:
                        sys.stderr.write(f"xh: error: failed to parse header value\n")
                        sys.exit(1)
                except (IOError, OSError) as e:
                    sys.stderr.write(f"xh: error: cannot read file '{filepath}': {e}\n")
                    sys.exit(1)
            headers.append((key, value))
        elif sep == ';':
            # Header with empty value
            headers.append((key, ''))
        else:
            sys.stderr.write(f"xh: error: failed to parse '{item}'\n")
            sys.exit(1)
    
    return headers, body_params, query_params, files, body_file


def parse_item(item):
    """Parse a single request item and return (key, separator, value)."""
    # Check for escape sequences
    # The separators in order of priority: :=, ==, =, @, :, ;
    
    # We need to handle backslash escapes
    # A backslash before a separator character escapes it
    
    # Find the first unescaped separator
    i = 0
    while i < len(item):
        if item[i] == '\\' and i + 1 < len(item):
            i += 2
            continue
        
        # Check for two-char separators first
        if i + 1 < len(item):
            two = item[i:i+2]
            if two == ':=':
                key = unescape(item[:i])
                value = item[i+2:]
                return key, ':=', value
            elif two == '==':
                key = unescape(item[:i])
                value = item[i+2:]
                return key, '==', value
        
        # Check for one-char separators
        ch = item[i]
        if ch == '=':
            key = unescape(item[:i])
            value = item[i+1:]
            return key, '=', value
        elif ch == '@':
            key = unescape(item[:i])
            value = item[i+1:]
            return key, '@', value
        elif ch == ':':
            key = unescape(item[:i])
            value = item[i+1:]
            return key, ':', value
        elif ch == ';':
            key = unescape(item[:i])
            value = item[i+1:]
            return key, ';', value
        
        i += 1
    
    return item, None, None


def unescape(s):
    """Remove backslash escapes from a string."""
    result = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(s):
        if s[i] == '\\' and i + 1 < len(s):
            result.append(s[i+1])
            i += 2
        else:
            result.append(s[i])
            i += 1
    return ''.join(result)


def normalize_url(url, https=False, default_scheme='http'):
    """Normalize the URL, handling localhost shorthand."""
    # Handle :// prefix (strip leading //)
    if url.startswith('://'):
        url = url[3:]
    
    # Handle :port or :/path shorthand for localhost
    if url.startswith(':'):
        rest = url[1:]
        if rest.startswith('/'):
            # :/path -> localhost/path
            url = f'localhost{url}'
        else:
            # :8080 or :8080/path -> localhost:8080[/path]
            url = f'localhost{url}'
    
    # Add scheme if missing
    if '://' not in url:
        # Check if the name suggests HTTPS
        scheme = default_scheme
        if https:
            scheme = 'https'
        url = f'{scheme}://{url}'
    
    return url


def build_json_body(body_params):
    """Build a JSON body from key-value pairs with nested JSON path support."""
    obj = {}
    for ptype, key, value in body_params:
        if ptype == 'string':
            _set_nested(obj, key, value)
        elif ptype == 'json':
            try:
                parsed = json.loads(value)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                sys.stderr.write(f"xh: error: '{value}' is not valid JSON\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            _set_nested(obj, key, parsed)
    
    return json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',', ':'))


def _set_nested(obj, key, value):
    """Set a value in a nested dict/list using HTTPie's JSON path syntax."""
    # Parse the key path: app[container][0][id]
    parts = _parse_key_path(key)
    
    if len(parts) == 1:
        obj[parts[0]] = value
        return
    
    # Navigate/create the path
    current = obj
    for i, part in enumerate(parts[:-1]):
        next_part = parts[i + 1]
        
        if isinstance(current, dict):
            if part not in current:
                # Create next level
                if isinstance(next_part, int):
                    current[part] = []
                else:
                    current[part] = {}
            current = current[part]
        elif isinstance(current, list):
            while len(current) <= part:
                # Determine what to fill with
                if isinstance(next_part, int):
                    current.append([])
                else:
                    current.append({})
            current = current[part]
    
    last = parts[-1]
    if isinstance(current, dict):
        current[last] = value
    elif isinstance(current, list):
        while len(current) <= last:
            current.append(None)
        current[last] = value


def _parse_key_path(key):
    """Parse a JSON path key like 'app[container][0][id]' into ['app', 'container', 0, 'id']."""
    parts = []
    # Split on [ and ]
    main = re.split(r'\[', key)
    
    if not main:
        return [key]
    
    parts.append(main[0])
    for part in main[1:]:
        part = part.rstrip(']')
        try:
            parts.append(int(part))
        except ValueError:
            parts.append(part)
    
    return parts


def build_form_body(body_params):
    """Build a URL-encoded form body."""
    params = []
    for ptype, key, value in body_params:
        if ptype == 'string':
            params.append((key, value))
        else:
            params.append((key, value))
    return urllib.parse.urlencode(params)


def build_multipart_body(body_params, files):
    """Build a multipart/form-data body."""
    boundary = f"{uuid.uuid4().hex[:16]}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:16]}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:16]}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:16]}"
    
    parts = []
    
    for ptype, key, value in body_params:
        parts.append(
            f'--{boundary}\r\n'
            f'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="{key}"\r\n'
            f'\r\n'
            f'{value}\r\n'
        )
    
    for key, filepath, mime_type, filename in files:
        if filename is None:
            filename = os.path.basename(filepath)
        
        if mime_type is None:
            mime_type, _ = mimetypes.guess_type(filepath)
        
        try:
            with open(filepath, 'rb') as f:
                file_data = f.read()
        except (IOError, OSError) as e:
            sys.stderr.write(f"xh: error: cannot read file '{filepath}': {e}\n")
            sys.exit(1)
        
        cd_line = f'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="{key}"; filename="{filename}"\r\n'
        ct_line = ''
        if mime_type:
            ct_line = f'Content-Type: {mime_type}\r\n'
        
        part = f'--{boundary}\r\n{cd_line}{ct_line}\r\n'.encode()
        part += file_data
        part += b'\r\n'
        parts.append(part)
    
    # Final boundary
    body_parts = []
    for p in parts:
        if isinstance(p, str):
            body_parts.append(p.encode())
        else:
            body_parts.append(p)
    
    final = f'--{boundary}--\r\n'.encode()
    body_parts.append(final)
    
    body = b''.join(body_parts)
    content_type = f'multipart/form-data; boundary={boundary}'
    
    return body, content_type


def deflate_compress(data):
    """Compress data using deflate."""
    return zlib.compress(data)[2:-4]  # Remove zlib header and checksum


def format_headers_block(status_line, headers_list, theme, do_color, do_format, sort_headers=True):
    """Format an HTTP headers block."""
    if do_format and sort_headers:
        headers_list = sorted(headers_list, key=lambda h: h[0].lower())
    
    lines = []
    if do_color:
        # Color the status line
        # Parse: "GET /path HTTP/1.1" or "HTTP/1.1 200 OK"
        if status_line.startswith('HTTP'):
            # Response
            m = re.match(r'HTTP/(\S+)\s+(\d+)\s*(.*)', status_line)
            if m:
                lines.append(colorize_response_line(m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(3), theme))
            else:
                lines.append(status_line)
        else:
            # Request
            parts = status_line.split(' ', 2)
            if len(parts) == 3:
                method, path, http = parts
                ver = http.replace('HTTP/', '')
                lines.append(colorize_request_line(method, path, ver, theme))
            else:
                lines.append(status_line)
        
        # Color headers
        t = get_theme(theme)
        r = t["reset"]
        for name, value in headers_list:
            lines.append(colorize_header(name, value, theme).rstrip('\n'))
        
        # Empty line after headers
        lines.append(f"{t['reset']}")
    else:
        lines.append(status_line)
        for name, value in headers_list:
            lines.append(f"{name}: {value}")
        lines.append("")
    
    return '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'


def print_output(data, content_type, is_headers_block, theme, do_color, do_format,
                 sort_headers=True, json_indent=4, json_format=True, stream=sys.stdout, is_request=False):
    """Print formatted output."""
    if is_headers_block:
        # data is (status_line, headers_list)
        status_line, headers_list = data
        output = format_headers_block(status_line, headers_list, theme, do_color, do_format, sort_headers)
        if hasattr(stream, 'buffer'):
            stream.buffer.write(output.encode('utf-8', errors='replace'))
        else:
            stream.write(output)
        return
    
    # Body data
    if isinstance(data, bytes):
        # Check if it's text
        if is_text_content_type(content_type):
            try:
                text = data.decode('utf-8')
            except UnicodeDecodeError:
                try:
                    text = data.decode('latin-1')
                except:
                    # Binary data
                    msg = "+-----------------------------------------+\n| NOTE: binary data not shown in terminal |\n+-----------------------------------------+\n"
                    if hasattr(stream, 'buffer'):
                        stream.buffer.write(msg.encode())
                    else:
                        stream.write(msg)
                    return
        else:
            # Binary data
            msg = "+-----------------------------------------+\n| NOTE: binary data not shown in terminal |\n+-----------------------------------------+\n"
            if hasattr(stream, 'buffer'):
                stream.buffer.write(msg.encode())
            else:
                stream.write(msg)
            return
    else:
        text = data
    
    # Apply JSON formatting if applicable
    if is_json_content_type(content_type) and json_format and do_format:
        formatted = format_json(text, indent=json_indent)
    else:

    if do_color and is_json_content_type(content_type):

    # Ensure output ends with newline when formatting

    if hasattr(stream, 'buffer'):

def generate_man_page():
    """Generate the man page."""
    today = datetime.date.today().strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    with open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), 'doc', 'xh.1'), 'r') as f:

def parse_args(argv):
    """Parse command line arguments with special handling."""
    prog = os.path.basename(argv[0]) if argv else 'xh'
    args_list = argv[1:]
    
    # Load config default options
    config = load_config()
    default_options = config.get('default_options', [])
    if default_options:
        args_list = default_options + args_list
    
    parser = create_arg_parser()
    parser.prog = prog
    
    # Pre-process: handle 'help' as special command
    if args_list and args_list[0] == 'help':
        print_long_help(prog)
        sys.exit(0)
    
    # Try to parse, handling unknown args gracefully for --no-* options
    try:
        namespace, remaining = parser.parse_known_args(args_list)
    except SystemExit as e:
        sys.exit(e.code)
    
    # Handle --version
    if namespace.version:
        print(f"xh {VERSION}")
        print("-native-tls +rustls")
        sys.exit(0)
    
    # Handle --help
    if namespace.help:
        print_short_help(prog)
        sys.exit(0)
    
    # Handle --generate
    if namespace.generate:
        output = generate_completions(namespace.generate)
        sys.stdout.write(output)
        sys.exit(0)
    
    # If no positional args, show help
    if not hasattr(namespace, 'method_or_url') or not namespace.method_or_url:
        print_short_help(prog)
        sys.exit(0)
    
    return namespace, prog

def parse_args(argv):
    """Parse command line arguments with special handling."""
    prog = os.path.basename(argv[0]) if argv else 'xh'
    args_list = argv[1:]
    
    # Load config default options
    config = load_config()
    default_options = config.get('default_options', [])
    if default_options:
        args_list = default_options + args_list
    
    parser = create_arg_parser()
    parser.prog = prog
    
    # Pre-process: handle 'help' as special command
    if args_list and args_list[0] == 'help':
        print_long_help(prog)
        sys.exit(0)
    
    # Try to parse, handling unknown args gracefully for --no-* options
    try:
        namespace, remaining = parser.parse_known_args(args_list)
    except SystemExit as e:
        sys.exit(e.code)
    
    # Handle --version
    if namespace.version:
        print(f"xh {VERSION}")
        print("-native-tls +rustls")
        sys.exit(0)
    
    # Handle --help
    if namespace.help:
        print_short_help(prog)
        sys.exit(0)
    
    # Handle --generate
    if namespace.generate:
        output = generate_completions(namespace.generate)
        sys.stdout.write(output)
        sys.exit(0)
    
    # If no positional args, show help
    if not hasattr(namespace, 'method_or_url') or not namespace.method_or_url:
        print_short_help(prog)
        sys.exit(0)
    
    return namespace, prog

def header_name_to_canonical(name):
    """Convert a header name to canonical form (Title-Case)."""
    return '-'.join(part.capitalize() for part in name.split('-'))


def detect_is_tty():
    """Detect if stdout is a terminal."""
    return sys.stdout.isatty()


def main():
    argv = sys.argv
    prog = os.path.basename(argv[0])
    
    # Determine if running in HTTPie compat mode
    httpie_compat = (
        prog in ('http', 'https') or
        os.environ.get('XH_HTTPIE_COMPAT_MODE', '').lower() in ('1', 'true', 'yes')
    )
    
    # Determine if https by default
    force_https = prog in ('xhs', 'https', 'xhttps')
    
    args_list = argv[1:]
    
    # Handle 'help' subcommand
    if args_list and args_list[0] == 'help':
        print_long_help(prog)
        sys.exit(0)
    
    # Load config default options
    config = load_config()
    default_options = config.get('default_options', [])
    if default_options:
        args_list = default_options + args_list
    
    # Parse arguments
    parser = create_arg_parser()
    parser.prog = prog
    
    try:
        namespace, remaining = parser.parse_known_args(args_list)
    except SystemExit:
        # Print minimal error
        sys.exit(1)
    
    # Handle --version
    if namespace.version:
        print(f"xh {VERSION}")
        print("-native-tls +rustls")
        sys.exit(0)
    
    # Handle --help
    if namespace.help:
        print_short_help(prog)
        sys.exit(0)
    
    # Handle --generate
    if namespace.generate:
        try:
            output = generate_completions(namespace.generate)
            sys.stdout.write(output)
        except Exception as e:
            sys.stderr.write(f"{prog}: error: {e}\n")
            sys.exit(1)
        sys.exit(0)
    
    # Check we have a URL
    if not namespace.method_or_url:
        print_short_help(prog)
        sys.exit(0)
    
    # Determine method and URL
    method_or_url = namespace.method_or_url
    request_items = namespace.request_items + remaining
    
    # Check if first arg is a method
    http_methods = {'GET', 'POST', 'PUT', 'DELETE', 'PATCH', 'HEAD', 'OPTIONS', 
                    'CONNECT', 'TRACE', 'get', 'post', 'put', 'delete', 'patch', 
                    'head', 'options', 'connect', 'trace'}
    
    method = None
    url_str = None
    
    # Check if first arg looks like a method
    if method_or_url.upper() in http_methods:
        method = method_or_url.upper()
        if request_items:
            url_str = request_items[0]
            request_items = request_items[1:]
        else:
            sys.stderr.write(f"{prog}: error: URL is required\n")
            sys.exit(1)
    else:
        url_str = method_or_url
    
    # Determine format options
    format_options = {}
    if namespace.format_options:
        for opt in namespace.format_options.split(','):
            opt = opt.strip()
            if ':' in opt:
                k, _, v = opt.partition(':')
                format_options[k.strip()] = v.strip()
    
    json_indent = int(format_options.get('json.indent', 4))
    json_format = format_options.get('json.format', 'true').lower() != 'false'
    headers_sort = format_options.get('headers.sort', 'true').lower() != 'false'
    
    # Determine pretty mode
    is_tty = detect_is_tty()
    no_color = bool(os.environ.get('NO_COLOR'))
    
    if namespace.pretty:
        pretty = namespace.pretty
    elif no_color:
        pretty = 'format'
    elif is_tty:
        pretty = 'all'
    else:
        pretty = 'none'
    
    do_color = pretty in ('all', 'colors')
    do_format = pretty in ('all', 'format')
    
    theme = namespace.style or 'auto'
    
    # Determine what to print
    print_format = namespace.print_format
    
    if namespace.verbose >= 1:
        print_format = 'HhBb'
        if namespace.verbose >= 2:
            print_format = 'HhBbm'
        if not namespace.show_all:
            namespace.show_all = True
    
    if namespace.headers:
        print_format = 'h'
    elif namespace.body:
        print_format = 'b'
    elif namespace.meta:
        print_format = 'm'
    
    if not print_format:
        print_format = 'hb'
    
    print_req_headers = 'H' in print_format
    print_req_body = 'B' in print_format
    print_resp_headers = 'h' in print_format
    print_resp_body = 'b' in print_format
    print_meta = 'm' in print_format
    
    # History print format
    history_print = namespace.history_print
    if namespace.verbose >= 1:
        history_print = 'HhBb'
    if not history_print:
        history_print = print_format
    
    hist_req_headers = 'H' in history_print
    hist_req_body = 'B' in history_print
    hist_resp_headers = 'h' in history_print
    hist_resp_body = 'b' in history_print
    
    # Parse request items
    is_form = bool(namespace.form)
    is_multipart = bool(namespace.multipart)
    is_json = bool(namespace.json)
    
    # Detect body from stdin
    ignore_stdin = namespace.ignore_stdin
    stdin_body = None
    
    if not ignore_stdin and not sys.stdin.isatty():
        # Read from stdin
        try:
            stdin_data = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
            if stdin_data:
                stdin_body = stdin_data
        except Exception:
            pass
    
    # Parse request items
    try:
        extra_headers, body_params, query_params, files, body_file = parse_request_items(
            request_items, is_form, is_multipart, is_json
        )
    except SystemExit:
        raise
    except Exception as e:
        sys.stderr.write(f"{prog}: error: {e}\n")
        sys.exit(1)
    
    # Determine body
    has_body_data = bool(body_params or files or namespace.raw or body_file)
    
    # Check for conflicting stdin usage
    if stdin_body is not None and has_body_data:
        sys.stderr.write(f"{prog}: error: Request body (from stdin) and request data (key=value) cannot be mixed. Pass --ignore-stdin to ignore standard input.\n")
        sys.exit(1)
    
    # Determine the default method
