    # Determine format options
    format_options = {}
    if namespace.format_options:
        for opt in namespace.format_options.split(','):
            opt = opt.strip()
            if ':' in opt:
                k, _, v = opt.partition(':')
                format_options[k.strip()] = v.strip()
    
    json_indent = int(format_options.get('json.indent', 4))
    json_format = format_options.get('json.format', 'true').lower() != 'false'
    headers_sort = format_options.get('headers.sort', 'true').lower() != 'false'
    
    # Determine pretty mode
    is_tty = detect_is_tty()
    no_color = bool(os.environ.get('NO_COLOR'))
    
    if namespace.pretty:
        pretty = namespace.pretty
    elif no_color:
        pretty = 'format'
    elif is_tty:
        pretty = 'all'
    else:
        pretty = 'none'
    
    do_color = pretty in ('all', 'colors')
    do_format = pretty in ('all', 'format')
    
    theme = namespace.style or 'auto'
    
    # Determine what to print
    print_format = namespace.print_format
    
    if namespace.verbose >= 1:
        print_format = 'HhBb'
        if namespace.verbose >= 2:
            print_format = 'HhBbm'
        if not namespace.show_all:
            namespace.show_all = True
    
    if namespace.headers:
        print_format = 'h'
    elif namespace.body:
        print_format = 'b'
    elif namespace.meta:
        print_format = 'm'
    
    if not print_format:
        print_format = 'hb'
    
    print_req_headers = 'H' in print_format
    print_req_body = 'B' in print_format
    print_resp_headers = 'h' in print_format
    print_resp_body = 'b' in print_format
    print_meta = 'm' in print_format
    
    # History print format
    history_print = namespace.history_print
    if namespace.verbose >= 1:
        history_print = 'HhBb'
    if not history_print:
        history_print = print_format
    
    hist_req_headers = 'H' in history_print
    hist_req_body = 'B' in history_print
    hist_resp_headers = 'h' in history_print
    hist_resp_body = 'b' in history_print
    
    # Parse request items
    is_form = bool(namespace.form)
    is_multipart = bool(namespace.multipart)
    is_json = bool(namespace.json)
    
    # Detect body from stdin
    ignore_stdin = namespace.ignore_stdin
    stdin_body = None
    
    if not ignore_stdin and not sys.stdin.isatty():
        # Read from stdin
        try:
            stdin_data = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
            if stdin_data:
                stdin_body = stdin_data
        except Exception:
            pass
    
    # Parse request items
    try:
        extra_headers, body_params, query_params, files, body_file = parse_request_items(
            request_items, is_form, is_multipart, is_json
        )
    except SystemExit:
        raise
    except Exception as e:
        sys.stderr.write(f"{prog}: error: {e}\n")
        sys.exit(1)
    
    # Determine body
    has_body_data = bool(body_params or files or namespace.raw or body_file)
    
    # Check for conflicting stdin usage
    if stdin_body is not None and has_body_data:
        sys.stderr.write(f"{prog}: error: Request body (from stdin) and request data (key=value) cannot be mixed. Pass --ignore-stdin to ignore standard input.\n")
        sys.exit(1)
    
    # Determine the default method
    if method is None:
        if has_body_data or stdin_body is not None:
            method = 'POST'
        else:
            method = 'GET'
    
    # Normalize URL
    default_scheme = namespace.default_scheme or ('https' if force_https else 'http')
    if namespace.https:
        default_scheme = 'https'
    
    url_str = normalize_url(url_str, default_scheme == 'https', default_scheme)
    
    # Parse URL and add query params
    parsed_url = urllib.parse.urlparse(url_str)
    
    # Extract auth from URL if present
    url_auth = None
    if parsed_url.username:
        url_auth = (parsed_url.username, parsed_url.password or '')
        # Remove auth from URL
        netloc = parsed_url.hostname
        if parsed_url.port:
            netloc += f':{parsed_url.port}'
        parsed_url = parsed_url._replace(netloc=netloc, username=None, password=None)
    
    # Add query params
    existing_params = urllib.parse.parse_qsl(parsed_url.query, keep_blank_values=True)
    all_params = existing_params + query_params
    if all_params:
        new_query = urllib.parse.urlencode(all_params)
        parsed_url = parsed_url._replace(query=new_query)
    
    url = urllib.parse.urlunparse(parsed_url)
    
    # Ensure path
    if not parsed_url.path:
        parsed_url = parsed_url._replace(path='/')
        url = urllib.parse.urlunparse(parsed_url)
    
    # Build request headers
    req_headers = {}
    req_headers['Accept-Encoding'] = 'gzip, deflate, br, zstd'
    req_headers['User-Agent'] = USER_AGENT
    req_headers['Connection'] = 'keep-alive'
    
    # Load session
    session_file = namespace.session or namespace.session_read_only
    session_data = None
    cookie_jar = []
    
    if session_file:
        session_data = load_session(session_file)
        # Apply session headers
        for sh in session_data.get('headers', []):
            req_headers[sh['name']] = sh['value']
        # Load session cookies
        cookie_jar = list(session_data.get('cookies', []))
        # Load session auth
        sess_auth = session_data.get('auth', {})
        if sess_auth.get('type') and not namespace.auth_type:
            namespace.auth_type = sess_auth['type']
            namespace.auth = sess_auth.get('raw_auth')
    
    # Apply extra headers from request items
    headers_to_remove = set()
    for name, value in extra_headers:
        if value == '':
            if name.lower() != '':
                # Check if removing header (name:)
                # value is '' but from : separator, means remove
                headers_to_remove.add(name.lower())
            else:
                req_headers[header_name_to_canonical(name)] = ''
        else:
            req_headers[header_name_to_canonical(name)] = value
    
    # Actually, we need to re-examine this: 
    # "header:" means remove header (value is empty after colon)
    # "header;" means header with empty value
    # Both are handled in parse_request_items as sep ':' and sep ';'
    # For ':' with empty value, we should remove the header
    # Let me re-check - in parse_item, ':' separator with empty value means unset
    for name, value in extra_headers:
        canonical = header_name_to_canonical(name)
        if value == '' and any(item.endswith(':') or 
                               (item.startswith(name + ':') and item[len(name)+1:] == '') 
                               for item in request_items):
            headers_to_remove.add(canonical.lower())
    
    # Remove headers marked for removal
    for k in list(req_headers.keys()):
        if k.lower() in headers_to_remove:
            del req_headers[k]
    
    # Determine body and content type
    body_bytes = None
    content_type = None
    
    if namespace.raw is not None:
        body_bytes = namespace.raw.encode('utf-8')
        # Content-type depends on mode
        if is_form:
            content_type = 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded'
        else:
            content_type = 'application/json'
    elif body_file:
        try:
            with open(body_file, 'rb') as f:
                body_bytes = f.read()
        except (IOError, OSError) as e:
            sys.stderr.write(f"{prog}: error: cannot read file '{body_file}': {e}\n")
            sys.exit(1)
        # No content-type set automatically for raw file body
    elif stdin_body is not None:
        body_bytes = stdin_body
        # Detect content type based on mode
        if is_form:
            content_type = 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded'
        else:
            content_type = 'application/json'
    elif body_params or files:
        if is_multipart or files:
            body_bytes, content_type = build_multipart_body(body_params, files)
        elif is_form:
            body_str = build_form_body(body_params)
            body_bytes = body_str.encode('utf-8')
            content_type = 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded'
        else:
            # JSON (default)
            body_str = build_json_body(body_params)
            body_bytes = body_str.encode('utf-8')
            content_type = 'application/json'
    
    # Set Accept header
    if is_json or (not is_form and not is_multipart and (body_params or namespace.json or 
                    stdin_body is not None or namespace.raw is not None)):
        if not any(k.lower() == 'accept' for k in req_headers):
            req_headers['Accept'] = 'application/json, */*;q=0.5'
    else:
        if not any(k.lower() == 'accept' for k in req_headers):
            req_headers['Accept'] = '*/*'
    
    # Override accept for explicit -j flag even without data
    if is_json:
        if not any(k.lower() == 'accept' for k in req_headers):
            req_headers['Accept'] = 'application/json, */*;q=0.5'
    
    # Set Content-Type
    if content_type:
        if not any(k.lower() == 'content-type' for k in req_headers):
            req_headers['Content-Type'] = content_type
    elif is_json and not body_bytes and not is_form:
        # Explicit -j with no body
        req_headers['Content-Type'] = 'application/json'
    elif is_form and not body_bytes:
        # Explicit -f with no body
        req_headers['Content-Type'] = 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded'
    
    # Handle auth
    auth_type = namespace.auth_type
    auth_creds = namespace.auth
    
    if namespace.bearer:
        auth_type = 'bearer'
        auth_creds = namespace.bearer
    
    # Apply URL auth
    if url_auth and not auth_creds:
        auth_type = 'basic'
        auth_creds = f"{url_auth[0]}:{url_auth[1]}"
    
    # Apply netrc auth
    if not auth_creds and not namespace.ignore_netrc:
        host = parsed_url.hostname
        netrc_auth = get_netrc_auth(host)
        if netrc_auth:
            auth_type = 'basic'
            auth_creds = f"{netrc_auth[0]}:{netrc_auth[1]}"
    
    # Add auth header to request headers
    if auth_type == 'basic' and auth_creds:
        if ':' in auth_creds:
            user, passwd = auth_creds.split(':', 1)
        else:
            user, passwd = auth_creds, ''
        cred = base64.b64encode(f"{user}:{passwd}".encode()).decode()
        req_headers['Authorization'] = f'Basic {cred}'
    elif auth_type == 'bearer' and auth_creds:
        req_headers['Authorization'] = f'Bearer {auth_creds}'
    
    # Add Content-Length and Host
    host_header = parsed_url.netloc
    if not any(k.lower() == 'host' for k in req_headers):
        req_headers['Host'] = host_header
    
    # Handle -j with no body (only Content-Type, no Content-Length)
    if is_json and not body_bytes and not is_form:
        pass  # Don't set Content-Length
    
    if body_bytes is not None and not any(k.lower() == 'content-length' for k in req_headers):
        req_headers['Content-Length'] = str(len(body_bytes))
    elif is_form and not body_bytes:
        # -f with no body
        req_headers['Content-Length'] = '0'
    
    # Handle compression
    compress_level = namespace.compress
    if compress_level > 0 and body_bytes:
        # Check if Content-Encoding already set by user
        if not any(k.lower() == 'content-encoding' for k in extra_headers):
            compressed = deflate_compress(body_bytes)
            # If compression ratio is negative, skip unless forced (compress > 1)
            if len(compressed) < len(body_bytes) or compress_level > 1:
                body_bytes = compressed
                req_headers['Content-Encoding'] = 'deflate'
                req_headers['Content-Length'] = str(len(body_bytes))
    
    # Build path for display
    display_path = parsed_url.path or '/'
    if parsed_url.query:
        display_path += '?' + parsed_url.query
    
    # Determine HTTP version string for request line
    http_ver_str = get_http_version_str(namespace.http_version)
    
    # Build request line
    request_line = f"{method} {display_path} HTTP/{http_ver_str}"
    
    # Build headers list in order
    headers_list = list(req_headers.items())
    
    # Check --curl mode
    if namespace.curl:
        # Warn about ignored options
        if namespace.offline:
            sys.stderr.write("Warning: Ignored --offline\n")
        if namespace.print_format:
            sys.stderr.write("Warning: Ignored -p/--print\n")
        
        # Parse proxies
        proxies_list = []
        if namespace.proxies:
            for proxy_spec in namespace.proxies:
                colon_idx = proxy_spec.find(':')
                if colon_idx > 0:
                    protocol = proxy_spec[:colon_idx]
                    proxy_url = proxy_spec[colon_idx+1:]
                    proxies_list.append((protocol, proxy_url))
        
        # Filter headers - don't include auto-set headers like User-Agent, Accept-Encoding, Connection, Host
        curl_headers = []
        auto_headers = {'user-agent', 'accept-encoding', 'connection', 'host', 'content-length', 'accept'}
        for name, value in headers_list:
            if name.lower() not in auto_headers:
                curl_headers.append((name, value))
        
        # Determine form params for curl
        curl_form_params = None
        if is_form and body_params and not is_multipart:
            curl_form_params = [(k, v) for _, k, v in body_params]
            body_bytes = None
        
        # Build resolve entries with port
        curl_resolve = []
        if namespace.resolve:
            parsed_port = parsed_url.port or (443 if parsed_url.scheme == 'https' else 80)
            for r in namespace.resolve:
                if ':' in r:
                    rhost, raddr = r.rsplit(':', 1)
                    curl_resolve.append(f"{rhost}:{parsed_port}:{raddr}")
        
        cmd = build_curl_command(
            method=method,
            url=url,
            headers=curl_headers,
            body=body_bytes,
            auth=auth_creds,
            auth_type=auth_type,
            proxies=proxies_list,
            verify=namespace.verify,
            cert=namespace.cert,
            cert_key=namespace.cert_key,
            ssl_version=namespace.ssl,
            timeout=namespace.timeout,
            follow=namespace.follow,
            max_redirects=namespace.max_redirects,
            ipv4=namespace.ipv4,
            ipv6=namespace.ipv6,
            http_version=namespace.http_version,
            unix_socket=namespace.unix_socket,
            resolve=curl_resolve,
            interface=namespace.interface,
            form_params=curl_form_params,
            is_download=namespace.download,
            output_file=namespace.output,
            long=namespace.curl_long,
        )
        
        print(cmd)
        sys.exit(0)
    
    # Offline mode - just print the request
    if namespace.offline:
        if namespace.quiet == 0:
            stdout = sys.stdout
            
            if print_req_headers:
                block = format_headers_block(request_line, headers_list, theme, do_color, do_format, headers_sort)
                if hasattr(stdout, 'buffer'):
                    stdout.buffer.write(block.encode('utf-8', errors='replace'))
                else:
                    stdout.write(block)
            
            if print_req_body:
                if body_bytes is not None:
                    # Determine content type for request
                    req_ct = req_headers.get('Content-Type', '')
                    for k, v in req_headers.items():
                        if k.lower() == 'content-type':
                            req_ct = v
                            break
                    
                    is_binary = False
                    if req_headers.get('Content-Encoding') == 'deflate':
                        is_binary = True
                    
                    if is_binary:
                        print_binary_notice(stdout)
                    else:
                        print_output(body_bytes, req_ct, False, theme, do_color, do_format,
                                     headers_sort, json_indent, json_format, stdout, is_request=True)
                else:
                    # No body - just a newline
                    if hasattr(stdout, 'buffer'):
                        stdout.buffer.write(b'\n')
                    else:
                        stdout.write('\n')
        
        sys.exit(0)
    
    # Prepare proxies
    proxies_list = []
    if namespace.proxies:
        for proxy_spec in namespace.proxies:
            colon_idx = proxy_spec.find(':')
            if colon_idx > 0:
                protocol = proxy_spec[:colon_idx]
                proxy_url = proxy_spec[colon_idx+1:]
                proxies_list.append((protocol, proxy_url))
    
    # Determine check_status
    if httpie_compat:
        check_status = namespace.check_status if namespace.check_status is not None else False
    else:
        check_status = namespace.check_status if namespace.check_status is not None else True
    
    # Output stream
    output_stream = sys.stdout
    output_file_handle = None
    
    if namespace.output and not namespace.download:
        try:
            output_file_handle = open(namespace.output, 'wb')
            output_stream = output_file_handle
        except (IOError, OSError) as e:
            sys.stderr.write(f"{prog}: error: cannot open output file '{namespace.output}': {e}\n")
            sys.exit(1)
    
    try:
        # Download mode
        if namespace.download:
            # For download, we print headers to stdout and save body to file
            download_headers = dict(req_headers)
            download_headers['Accept-Encoding'] = 'identity'
            
            # Print request headers if needed
            if namespace.quiet == 0 and print_req_headers:
                block = format_headers_block(request_line, headers_list, theme, do_color, do_format, headers_sort)
                if hasattr(sys.stdout, 'buffer'):
                    sys.stdout.buffer.write(block.encode('utf-8', errors='replace'))
                else:
                    sys.stdout.write(block)
            
            # Make request and download
            try:
                response, elapsed = make_request(
                    method=method,
                    url=url,
                    headers=download_headers,
                    body=body_bytes,
                    timeout=namespace.timeout,
                    verify=namespace.verify,
                    cert=namespace.cert,
                    cert_key=namespace.cert_key,
                    ssl_version=namespace.ssl,
                    http_version=namespace.http_version,
                    proxies=proxies_list if proxies_list else None,
                    unix_socket=namespace.unix_socket,
                    resolve=namespace.resolve,
                    interface=namespace.interface,
                    ipv4=namespace.ipv4,
                    ipv6=namespace.ipv6,
                    follow_redirects=True,
                    max_redirects=namespace.max_redirects or 30,
                    cookie_jar=cookie_jar if session_data is not None else None,
                )
            except (ConnectionError, TimeoutError) as e:
                sys.stderr.write(f"{prog}: error: {e}\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            
            # Print response headers
            if namespace.quiet == 0 and print_resp_headers:
                resp_status_line = f"HTTP/{response.http_version} {response.status_code} {response.status_text}"
                resp_headers_list = list(response.headers)
                block = format_headers_block(resp_status_line, resp_headers_list, theme, do_color, do_format, headers_sort)
                if hasattr(sys.stdout, 'buffer'):
                    sys.stdout.buffer.write(block.encode('utf-8', errors='replace'))
                else:
                    sys.stdout.write(block)
            
            # Save body to file
            output_path = namespace.output
            if not output_path:
                # Get from Content-Disposition or URL
                cd = dict(response.headers).get('Content-Disposition', '')
                if cd and 'filename=' in cd:
                    m = re.search(r'filename="?([^";]+)"?', cd)
                    if m:
                        output_path = m.group(1)
                
                if not output_path:
                    path = urllib.parse.urlparse(url).path
                    output_path = os.path.basename(path) or 'index.html'
            
            total = len(response.body)
            
            if namespace.quiet == 0:
                sys.stderr.write(f'Downloading {format_size(total)} to "{output_path}"\n')
                sys.stderr.flush()
            
            mode = 'ab' if namespace.resume and os.path.exists(output_path) else 'wb'
            with open(output_path, mode) as f:
                f.write(response.body)
            
            if namespace.quiet == 0:
                speed = total / elapsed if elapsed > 0 else 0
                sys.stderr.write(f'Done. {format_size(total)} in {elapsed:.5f}s ({format_size(speed)}/s)\n')
                sys.stderr.flush()
            
            sys.exit(0)
        
        # Regular request
        # Print request headers if needed
        if namespace.quiet == 0 and print_req_headers:
            block = format_headers_block(request_line, headers_list, theme, do_color, do_format, headers_sort)
            if hasattr(output_stream, 'buffer'):
                output_stream.buffer.write(block.encode('utf-8', errors='replace'))
            elif hasattr(output_stream, 'write'):
                output_stream.write(block)
        
        # Print request body if needed
        if namespace.quiet == 0 and print_req_body and body_bytes is not None:
            req_ct = ''
            for k, v in req_headers.items():
                if k.lower() == 'content-type':
                    req_ct = v
                    break
            
            is_binary_body = req_headers.get('Content-Encoding') == 'deflate'
            
            if is_binary_body:
                print_binary_notice(output_stream if not isinstance(output_stream, io.IOBase) or hasattr(output_stream, 'mode') else sys.stdout)
            else:
                print_output(body_bytes, req_ct, False, theme, do_color, do_format,
                             headers_sort, json_indent, json_format, 
                             output_stream if not isinstance(output_stream, (io.RawIOBase, io.BufferedIOBase)) else sys.stdout,
                             is_request=True)
        
        # Make the actual request
        try:
            response, elapsed = make_request(
                method=method,
                url=url,
                headers=req_headers,
                body=body_bytes,
                timeout=namespace.timeout,
                verify=namespace.verify,
                cert=namespace.cert,
                cert_key=namespace.cert_key,
                ssl_version=namespace.ssl,
                http_version=namespace.http_version,
                proxies=proxies_list if proxies_list else None,
                unix_socket=namespace.unix_socket,
                resolve=namespace.resolve,
                interface=namespace.interface,
                ipv4=namespace.ipv4,
                ipv6=namespace.ipv6,
                follow_redirects=namespace.follow,
                max_redirects=namespace.max_redirects or 30,
                cookie_jar=cookie_jar if session_data is not None else None,
            )
        except ConnectionError as e:
            sys.stderr.write(f"{prog}: error: {e}\n")
            sys.exit(1)
        except TimeoutError as e:
            sys.stderr.write(f"{prog}: error: {e}\n")
            sys.exit(2)
        
        # Update session
        if session_data is not None and namespace.session:
            # Update cookies
            session_data['cookies'] = cookie_jar
            # Update auth
            if auth_type and auth_creds:
                session_data['auth'] = {
                    'type': auth_type,
                    'raw_auth': auth_creds
                }
            try:
                save_session(namespace.session, session_data)
            except SystemExit:
                raise
        
        # Print response headers
        resp_status_line = f"HTTP/{response.http_version} {response.status_code} {response.status_text}"
        resp_headers_list = list(response.headers)
        
        # Check status
        status_code = response.status_code
        
        # Issue warning for error status codes
        if check_status and namespace.quiet < 2:
            if status_code >= 400:
                status_text = response.status_text
                sys.stderr.write(f"{prog}: warning: HTTP {status_code} {status_text}\n")
        
        if namespace.quiet == 0:
            if print_resp_headers:
                block = format_headers_block(resp_status_line, resp_headers_list, theme, do_color, do_format, headers_sort)
                if isinstance(output_stream, (io.RawIOBase, io.BufferedIOBase)):
                    output_stream.write(block.encode('utf-8', errors='replace'))
                elif hasattr(output_stream, 'buffer'):
                    output_stream.buffer.write(block.encode('utf-8', errors='replace'))
                else:
                    output_stream.write(block)
            
            if print_resp_body:
                resp_ct = ''
                for k, v in response.headers:
                    if k.lower() == 'content-type':
                        resp_ct = v
                        break
                
                if namespace.response_mime:
                    resp_ct = namespace.response_mime
                
                resp_body = response.body
                
                # Handle response charset
                if namespace.response_charset:
                    try:
                        resp_body_text = resp_body.decode(namespace.response_charset)
                        resp_body = resp_body_text.encode('utf-8')
                    except Exception:
                        pass
                
                if isinstance(output_stream, (io.RawIOBase, io.BufferedIOBase)):
                    # Write to file
                    output_stream.write(resp_body)
                else:
                    print_output(resp_body, resp_ct, False, theme, do_color, do_format,
                                 headers_sort, json_indent, json_format, output_stream)
            
            if print_meta:
                meta_lines = []
                meta_lines.append(f"Elapsed time: {elapsed:.5f}s")
                meta_lines.append(f"Remote address: {response.remote_addr}")
                meta_text = '\n'.join(meta_lines) + '\n\n'
                if isinstance(output_stream, (io.RawIOBase, io.BufferedIOBase)):
                    output_stream.write(meta_text.encode())
                elif hasattr(output_stream, 'buffer'):
                    output_stream.buffer.write(meta_text.encode())
                else:
                    output_stream.write(meta_text)
        
        # Determine exit code
        if check_status:
            if status_code >= 300 and status_code < 400:
                if output_file_handle:
                    output_file_handle.close()

def header_name_to_canonical(name):
    """Convert a header name to canonical form (Title-Case)."""
    return '-'.join(part.capitalize() for part in name.split('-'))

    return sys.stdout.isatty()

                sys.stderr.flush()
            
            mode = 'ab' if namespace.resume and os.path.exists(output_path) else 'wb'
            with open(output_path, mode) as f:
                f.write(response.body)
            
            if namespace.quiet == 0:
                speed = total / elapsed if elapsed > 0 else 0
                sys.stderr.write(f'Done. {format_size(total)} in {elapsed:.5f}s ({format_size(speed)}/s)\n')

            req_ct = ''

            else:

                verify=namespace.verify,

        except TimeoutError as e:

            sys.exit(2)
        
        # Update session

            # Update cookies
            session_data['cookies'] = cookie_jar
            # Update auth
            if auth_type and auth_creds:

        resp_headers_list = list(response.headers)

                if isinstance(output_stream, (io.RawIOBase, io.BufferedIOBase)):

# Key insights:
# JSON body: AE, UA, Conn, Accept(json), CT(json), CL, Host
# Form body: AE, UA, Conn, CT(form), Accept(*/*), CL, Host
# Custom headers for JSON: AE, UA, Conn, Accept, CT, Custom, CL, Host
# Custom headers for Form: AE, UA, Conn, CT, Custom, Accept, CL, Host
# Auth (-a) for GET: AE, UA, Conn, Auth, Accept, Host
# Auth (-a) for POST JSON: AE, UA, Conn, Accept, CT, Auth, CL, Host

# The pattern seems to be:
# For JSON mode: Accept comes BEFORE Content-Type
# For Form mode: Content-Type comes BEFORE Accept
# Custom headers come AFTER Content-Type (in form position)
# Auth (-a) comes in the "custom headers" zone

# Actually I think the real behavior is that xh uses reqwest's builder
# and the order is determined by when headers are inserted into reqwest's map

# The xh code adds headers in this order:
# 1. Set "default" headers on the client (AE, UA, Conn)
# 2. For JSON mode: add Accept=application/json first
# 3. Apply request-item headers (custom headers)
# 4. Add Content-Type from body 
# 5. Add Authorization
# 6. Body is set (reqwest adds Content-Length at actual send time)
# 7. Host is added by reqwest at network level

# But that doesn't match what we see...

# Let me look at this differently. Perhaps the order is:

# Custom Accept header from request items follows the position rules:
# - it goes in the "custom headers" slot (before the auto-added Accept)
# - but since it sets Accept, the auto Accept is not added separately

# Let me understand: when a user provides "accept:myaccept", it replaces the Accept header
# and the position depends on where in the custom headers it appears

# Actually, looking at the output, it seems like:
# - For "x-custom:yes accept:myaccept" - x-custom comes first, then Accept
# - For "accept:myaccept x-custom:yes" - Accept comes first, then x-custom
# So they maintain their relative order among themselves

# This means: all custom headers (including overrides of auto headers) are placed
# at the "custom headers" slot, maintaining their input order

# The auto headers (AE, UA, Conn, Accept) are placed:
# - For GET/no-body: [AE, UA, Conn] + [custom] + [Accept] + [Host]
# - But when user provides Accept in custom, it's placed IN the custom slot

# Actually the simpler explanation: 
# xh builds headers with specific logic:
# 1. Client-level headers (AE, UA, Conn) - always first
# 2. Then in one pass, adds:
#    - For JSON: Accept(json) and CT(json) together before request-item headers
#    - For Form: CT(form) before request-item headers, Accept(*/*) after
#    - Else: nothing before request-item headers
# 3. Request-item headers (custom headers + auth from items)
# 4. Auth from -a flag
# 5. Accept(*/*) for non-JSON mode (after request items)  
# 6. CL and CT from body (added by reqwest)
# 7. Host (last, by reqwest)

# I think the clearest model is:
# The headers are built as an ordered list:
# [AE, UA, Conn]
# + (if JSON mode): [Accept(json), CT(json)]
# + (if Form mode): [CT(form)]
# + (if auth from URL): [Auth] - but this was shown to be FIRST above Accept-Encoding
#   Actually, let me re-check URL auth

./executable --offline -I --print=H GET http://user:pass@example.com -j 2>&1

def _gen_fish(prog):
    content = _read_completion_file('xh.fish')
    if content:
        return content.replace('xh', prog)
    return f"# fish completion for {prog}\n"


def _gen_zsh(prog):
    content = _read_completion_file('_xh')
    if content:
        # Replace function name and program name
        content = re.sub(r'#compdef xh\b', f'#compdef {prog}', content)
        content = content.replace("'xh'", f"'{prog}'")
        content = content.replace('"xh"', f'"{prog}"')
        content = re.sub(r'\b_xh\b', f'_{prog}', content)
        return content
    return f"#compdef {prog}\n"


def _gen_elvish(prog):

def _gen_ps(prog):

    return f"# PowerShell completion for {prog}\n"


def _gen_nu(prog):
    content = _read_completion_file('xh.nu')

        return content.replace('xh', prog)
    return f"# nushell completion for {prog}\n"


def _gen_man(prog):
    today = datetime.date.today().strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    script_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    man_path = os.path.join(script_dir, 'doc', 'xh.1')
    if os.path.exists(man_path):
        with open(man_path, 'r') as f:
            content = f.read()
        # Update date
        content = re.sub(r'^\.TH XH 1 \S+', f'.TH XH 1 {today}', content, flags=re.MULTILINE)
        return content
    return f".TH {prog.upper()} 1 {today}\n"

# Body params: name=alice -> JSON -> CT: application/json, Accept: app/json...

# 2. Then implied headers (CT, Accept) in CT-first, Accept-second order
# 3. Then body

# This means the "implied" headers in curl come in CT-first order, different from request order

# This confirms: CT is hidden ONLY when using --data-urlencode

# Now I understand the complete curl building logic:
# The headers to include in -H are:
# 1. User item headers (custom) in order
# 2. If NOT form_params mode: CT (if it's not the default for --data-urlencode)
# 3. If JSON accept: Accept header
# (Auth is handled separately via --basic etc.)

# This is essentially: 
# - User item non-auto headers
# - Auto CT (unless form_params are used, in which case curl infers CT)
# - Auto Accept (if not */* )

# I need to restructure the curl generation to separate:
# - User-provided headers (from item_headers_filtered)
# - Auth (from -a flag)
# - Implied headers (CT, Accept) based on mode

# This requires passing more info to build_curl_cmd
# Let me restructure the curl call in main()

python3 << 'PYEOF'
with open('/workspace/xh_new.py', 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()

# Find and update the curl section in main()
old_curl_section = '''        # Build headers list for curl
        # build_curl_cmd will handle the filtering
        curl_headers = list(headers_ordered)'''

new_curl_section = '''        # For curl: separate headers into categories
        # 1. User item headers (custom, non-auto)
        curl_custom_headers = []
        for name, value in item_headers_filtered:
            if name.lower() not in ('accept-encoding', 'user-agent', 'connection', 'host', 'content-length'):
                curl_custom_headers.append((name, value))
        
        # 2. Implied headers (CT, Accept) 
        # - CT: include unless using form_params (which implies it via --data-urlencode)
        # - Accept: include if not */* (default)
        curl_implied_headers = []
        if not curl_form_params:
            # Include CT if set
            for name, value in headers_ordered:
                if name.lower() == 'content-type':
                    curl_implied_headers.append((name, value))
                    break
        
        # Include Accept if not */*
        for name, value in headers_ordered:
            if name.lower() == 'accept' and value != '*/*':
                curl_implied_headers.append((name, value))
                break
        
        # Combine: custom headers + implied headers
        # Auth is handled separately in build_curl_cmd
        curl_headers = curl_custom_headers + curl_implied_headers'''

content = content.replace(old_curl_section, new_curl_section, 1)
with open('/workspace/xh_new.py', 'w') as f:
    f.write(content)
print("Done")
PYEOF

r = conn.getresponse()
data = json.loads(r.read())
print('Connection:', data['headers'].get('Connection'))
"

# Two issues with download mode:
# 1. My implementation shows "Downloading" BEFORE headers, original shows AFTER headers
# 2. My implementation shows response headers first then download info, original reverses

# Looking at the original output order for download mode:
# HTTP/1.0 200 OK (response headers)
# [empty line]
# Downloading N B to "..."
# Done. N B in ...s (... MiB/s)

# My output:
# Downloading N B to "..."
# Done. N B in ...s
# HTTP/1.0 200 OK (response headers)

# The original shows headers first, THEN download progress
# The download progress goes to stderr but the headers go to stdout
# Let me verify: in the original, which stream gets what?

/workspace/executable -I http://127.0.0.1:18990/test -d --output=/tmp/test-dl.json 2>/dev/null
echo "=== stdout only ==="
/workspace/executable -I http://127.0.0.1:18990/test -d --output=/tmp/test-dl.json >/dev/null 2>&1
echo "exit: $?"

# space = R -> just add " "

    return f"{R}{t[\'header_name\']}{name}{R}{colon}:{R}{space_color} {R}{t[\'header_val\']}{value}{R}{nl}"'''

    t = get_theme(theme_name)

    nl = t[\'nl\']
    colon = t[\'colon\']

    def emit(color, text):

            return f"{text}{R}"

# 1. Auto theme header: extra ESC[0m at end of line (from nl_color=R being emitted)

#    Original solarized: GET{R}{245} {R}{245}/{R}{245} {R}{33}HTTP{R}{245}/{R}{37}1.1{R}{245}

#    The spaces between GET, /, HTTP are colored with the "url_path" color in original

# Let me analyze the request line format more carefully
# Solarized request line:
# R + 33m(method) + "GET" + R + 245(url_path) + " " + R + 245(url_path) + "/" + R + 245 + " " + R + 33(http_kw) + "HTTP" + R + 245(/) + "/" + R + 37(version) + "1.1" + R + 245(nl)

# That means:
# - Space after method: uses url_path color (245)
# - URL path: uses url_path color (245)
# - Space after URL: uses url_path color (245)
# - HTTP: uses http_kw color (33)
# - Slash in HTTP/1.1: uses...245? That's the url_path color again
# - Version: uses version color (37)
# - End: nl color (245)

# So the request line format in solarized:
# R + method_c + method + R + url_c + " " + R + url_c + path + R + url_c + " " + R + http_kw_c + "HTTP" + R + colon_c + "/" + R + version_c + ver + R + nl

# In monokai:
# Space uses nl color (15)
# URL path uses url_path color = 15 (same as nl)
# HTTP/ uses colon color 197
# Version uses version color 141

# Let me re-examine the themes to get the request line colors right:
# For each theme, what color do spaces around URL use?
# - auto: spaces use " " (reset/plain) 
# - solarized: spaces use url_path=245
# - monokai: spaces use nl=15
# - fruity: spaces use url_path=15 (same as nl)

# Wait, but the url_path and nl colors are different in some themes...

python3 -c "
import subprocess

    capture_output=True)
data = result.stdout
lines = data.split(b'\n')
for b in lines[0]:
    if b == 0x1b:
        print('ESC', end='')
    elif b < 32 and b != 10:
        print(f'[{b:02x}]', end='')
    else:
        print(chr(b), end='')
"

# R + 245 + {[NL] + R + 245 + "    " + R + 33 + " + R + 33 + name + R + 33 + " + R + 245 + ": " + R + 37 + "alice" + R + 245 + ,[NL] + R + 245 + "    " + R + 33 + " + ...

# Patterns:
# 1. {[NL] is ONE token with color 245 (punct color for solarized)
# 2. "    " (4 spaces) is one token with color 245 (punct color!)
# 3. ": " (colon + space) is ONE token with color 245 (punct color)
# 4. ,[NL] is ONE token with color 245 (punct color)
# 5. Trailing [NL] after } is 245 colored, then final } is 245, then final [NL] + R

# So the key insight: NEWLINES and spaces in JSON are treated as PUNCTUATION with the punct color
# This is because syntect's json-kv lexer puts newlines and whitespace in the punctuation scope!

# For auto theme (punct=R): R + {[NL] = R + { + NL (but with R, not without)
# Wait, for auto: R + { [NL] as one sequence:
# auto: R + {[NL] + R + "    " + R + 12m + "key" + R + ": " + R + 33m + "value" + R + [NL] + R + }[NL] + R + [NL] + R + [NL][NL]

# For auto: the whitespace/newline tokens are colored with R (punct=R), so they look like:
# R + whitespace + R = R + ws + R
# But adjacent R's collapse visually

# MY PROBLEM: I emit whitespace as PLAIN text (no color wrapping)
# Original: whitespace is wrapped in punct_color + ws + R

# THE FIX:
# For newlines and spaces: emit as punct_color + whitespace + R
# OR if in the middle of formatted output, wrap whitespace sequences with the punct color

# Let me update the colorize_json whitespace handling:
python3 << 'PYEOF'
with open('/workspace/xh.py', 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()

# Update whitespace handling in colorize_json
old = '''        elif ch in ' \\t\\n\\r':
            result.append(ch)'''

new = '''        elif ch in ' \\t\\n\\r':
            # Whitespace is treated as punctuation scope in syntect
            # For newlines/spaces in formatted JSON, use punct color
            p = t['json_punct']
            # Collect all consecutive whitespace
            j = i + 1
            while j < n and text[j] in ' \\t\\n\\r':
                j += 1
            ws = text[i:j]
            if p == R:
                result.append(ws)
            else:
                result.append(f"{p}{ws}{R}")
            i = j
            continue'''

content = content.replace(old, new, 1)

# Also: the punctuation that's followed by newlines (like { followed by \n)
# should be in the SAME token in the original
# But this is complex to fix at token level
# Let me check if just fixing whitespace handling is sufficient

with open('/workspace/xh.py', 'w') as f:
    f.write(content)
print("Done")
PYEOF

# Progress! But still differences:
# mine: R + 245 + { + R + 245 + [NL] + "    " + R + 33 + " + ...
#        ^(each punct token has its own R+245+...+R)  ^(NL+spaces as one token but not split right)
# orig: R + 245 + {[NL] + R + 245 + "    " + R + 33 + " + ...

# The main differences:
# 1. mine: { is one token (245+{+R), then [NL]+"    " is one token (245+[NL]    +R)
#    orig: {[NL] is one token (245+{[NL]+R), then "    " is its own token (245+"    "+R)
# 2. mine: colon and space are separate tokens (: R 245 SPACE R)
#    orig: ": " is one token (245+": "+R)
# 3. trailing: mine ends with R + } + R + [NL][NL]
#              orig ends with R + 245 + } + R + [NL] + R + 245 + [NL] + R + [NL][NL]

# The key issue: in the original, the JSON punctuation and ADJACENT whitespace are merged
# Specifically:
# - "{" + "\n" -> one token "{[NL]"
# - ":" + " " -> one token ": "
# - "," + "\n" -> one token ",[NL]"  
# - "\n" + "}" -> ??? (no, } is separate)
# - But trailing "\n" after } is 245

# This is because in xh's JSON lexer, the scope for "punctuation adjacent to whitespace"
# is handled as a combined token

# For my implementation, I need to merge punctuation with following whitespace:
# When I emit a punctuation char, check if the next char is whitespace
# If so, include all following whitespace in the same token

python3 << 'PYEOF'
with open('/workspace/xh.py', 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()

# Update punctuation handling to merge with adjacent whitespace
old = '''        elif ch in '{}[],:':
            p = t['json_punct']
            if p == R:
                result.append(f"{ch}{R}")
            else:
                result.append(f"{p}{ch}{R}")'''

new = '''        elif ch in '{}[],:':
            p = t['json_punct']
            # Merge punctuation with following whitespace (as syntect does)
            j = i + 1
            while j < n and text[j] in ' \\t\\n\\r':
                j += 1
            # But only merge newlines if they immediately follow the punctuation
            # Check if there's a newline immediately after (to handle {\\n pattern)
            following_ws = text[i+1:j]
            full_token = ch + following_ws
            if p == R:
                result.append(f"{full_token}{R}")
            else:
                result.append(f"{p}{full_token}{R}")
            i = j
            continue'''

# Also need to update whitespace handling: since punct now consumes following whitespace,
# the standalone whitespace that starts a line (indentation) is handled separately
# But wait - the indentation spaces (4 spaces at start of key line) DON'T come right after punctuation
# They come after the {[NL] token's newline
# So the 4 spaces would be caught by the "elif ch in ' \\t\\n\\r'" handler

content = content.replace(old, new, 1)
with open('/workspace/xh.py', 'w') as f:
    f.write(content)
print("Done")

# = warning[NL][NL]curl[NL] when combined

# So the difference: mine adds the blank line to STDOUT (before curl)
# Original adds the blank line to STDERR (after warnings)

# The fix: 
# 1. Remove the '\n' I added before curl in stdout
# 2. Add '\n' after each warning in curl mode (or after the last warning)

# Actually looking at the original's stderr output: 'Warning: Ignored --offline\n\n'
# This is TWO newlines, meaning the warning itself has a trailing newline AND there's an extra blank line
# But wait - when we use subprocess and get separate stdout/stderr, the stderr has that extra '\n'

# For the INTERACTIVE user (2>&1 view), it looks like:
# Warning (stderr)
# [blank line] (from extra \n in stderr)
# curl (stdout)

# For the automated test using stdout+stderr separately:
# stdout = 'curl...\n'
# stderr = 'Warning...\n\n'

# My implementation:
# stdout = '\ncurl...\n'  (extra leading newline)
# stderr = 'Warning...\n'

# The FIX:
# 1. Don't add '\n' before curl in stdout
# 2. After writing warnings to stderr, write an extra '\n' to stderr

python3 << 'PYEOF'
with open('/workspace/xh.py', 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()

# Find the curl warning and command output section
old = '''        if ns.offline:
            sys.stderr.write("Warning: Ignored --offline\\n")
        if ns.print_format:
            sys.stderr.write("Warning: Ignored -p/--print\\n")'''

new = '''        _curl_warned = False
        if ns.offline:
            sys.stderr.write("Warning: Ignored --offline\\n")
            _curl_warned = True
        if ns.print_format:
            sys.stderr.write("Warning: Ignored -p/--print\\n")
            _curl_warned = True
        if _curl_warned:
            sys.stderr.write("\\n")  # blank line after warnings'''

content = content.replace(old, new, 1)

# Remove the extra '\n' before curl command
old2 = '''        sys.stdout.write('\\n')
        sys.stdout.write(cmd + '\\n')'''

new2 = '''        sys.stdout.write(cmd + '\\n')'''

content = content.replace(old2, new2, 1)

with open('/workspace/xh.py', 'w') as f:
    f.write(content)
print("Done")
PYEOF

# Then: if not ends_with_\n: add '\n' -> adds '\n', then add '\n' (unconditionally)
# = }\n\n ✓

# if not ends_with_\n: False (already ends with \n) -> DON'T add '\n'
# then add '\n' (unconditionally) -> adds one '\n'
# = --BOUNDARY--\r\n\n

# The issue: multipart ends with '\r\n' which satisfies endswith('\n')
# So only ONE '\n' is added
# But JSON ends with '}' which doesn't satisfy endswith('\n'), so TWO '\n' are added

# = text += '\n\n' (unconditionally)
# For JSON: }\n\n (one line ending + one blank) 
# But orig JSON body: }\n\n ✓ (correct)

# For multipart: --BOUNDARY--\r\n + '\n\n' = --BOUNDARY--\r\n\n\n
# Orig: --BOUNDARY--\r\n\n\n ✓ (correct)

            if not text.endswith('\\n'):
                text += '\\n'
            text += '\\n'
        elif do_format:
            # Response body with format gets \\n\\n
            if not text.endswith('\\n'):

            if not text.endswith('\\n'):

            text += '\\n'

content = content.replace(old, new, 1)
with open('/workspace/xh.py', 'w') as f:
    f.write(content)
print("Done")

# mine: ...HTTP + R + "/" + R + 37m + "1.0"...
# orig: ...HTTP + R + 245m + "/" + R + 37m + "1.0"...

# In the response status line: HTTP/1.0 200 OK
# The "/" between HTTP and 1.0 uses:
# mine: R (no color = auto default)
# orig: 245m (solarized gray = colon color for solarized)

# My colorize_response_line:
# f"{R}{t['http_kw']}HTTP{R}/{R}{t['version']}{http_ver}{R}..."
# = R + http_kw(33m) + HTTP + R + "/" + R + version(37m) + "1.0"...

# The "/" should use the colon_color (which for solarized is 245m)
# But my code uses plain R for "/"

# Let me fix colorize_response_line to use colon color for "/":
python3 << 'PYEOF'
with open('/workspace/xh.py', 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()

old = '''def colorize_response_line(http_ver, status_code, status_text, theme_name):
    t = get_theme(theme_name)
    R = RESET
    return (
        f"{R}{t[\'http_kw\']}HTTP{R}/{R}{t[\'version\']}{http_ver}{R} "
        f"{R}{t[\'status_code\']}{status_code}{R} "
        f"{R}{t[\'status_text\']}{status_text}{R}"
    )'''

new = '''def colorize_response_line(http_ver, status_code, status_text, theme_name):
    t = get_theme(theme_name)
    R = RESET
    colon_c = t[\'colon\']
    nl_c = t[\'nl\']
    
    def e(color, text):
        if color == R:
            return f"{text}{R}"
        return f"{color}{text}{R}"
    
    # Response line: R + http_kw + HTTP + R + colon_c + "/" + R + version + http_ver + R + space + R + status_code + status + R + space + R + status_text + status + R + nl
    # Spaces around status: use nl_color (whitespace scope)
    return (
        f"{R}{t[\'http_kw\']}HTTP{R}"
        f"{e(colon_c, \'/\')}"
        f"{t[\'version\']}{http_ver}{R}"
        f"{e(nl_c, \' \')}"
        f"{t[\'status_code\']}{status_code}{R}"
        f"{e(nl_c, \' \')}"
        f"{t[\'status_text\']}{status_text}{R}"
        f"{nl_c if nl_c != R else \'\'}"
    )'''

content = content.replace(old, new, 1)
with open('/workspace/xh.py', 'w') as f:
    f.write(content)
print("Done")

import subprocess

def normalize(b):
    b = re.sub(b'Elapsed time: [0-9.]+s', b'Elapsed time: Xs', b)
    b = re.sub(b'Date: [^\n]+\n', b'', b)
    return b

def test(args):

# "body": "{\"name\":\"alice\"}"
# My code treats this as a string value (not further parsed)
# But the original PARSES the escaped JSON WITHIN the string!
#

# my code: treats as string value -> json_str color (e.g., ESC[33m for auto)
# orig: parses the JSON within the string -> applies JSON syntax coloring to the inner JSON!
#
# This is an advanced feature: xh's syntax highlighter recognizes nested JSON within strings
# and colors the inner structure with different colors
#
# Looking at the original for auto theme:
# ...ESC[33m"{ESC[0m ESC[34m\"...
# = string color + "{ + R + bool/num color + \"...
# 
# This is the json-kv lexer from xh which embeds JSON syntax in string values
# This is very complex to replicate exactly

# Let me check if this is the json-kv specific lexer behavior:
# The value "{\"name\":\"alice\"}" appears to be colorized with special JSON syntax
# The \" are colored differently from regular key quotes

# This would require implementing a full JSON lexer that recognizes embedded JSON
# It's very complex and the original behavior is a unique feature of syntect's json-kv lexer

# For now, let me check how often this occurs and whether to implement it
# The test case is: POST request that sends name=alice, response body contains the request body

# The response body has "body": "{\"name\":\"alice\"}" which is a JSON-encoded string
# The original xh parses the CONTENT of that string as JSON too!

# This is the json-kv lexer's special behavior:
# When a string value LOOKS like JSON (starts with { or [), it colorizes it as nested JSON

# Let me check: does this happen for ALL JSON strings or just some?
python3 -c "
import subprocess, re
orig_r = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', '--offline', '-I', '--print=B', 'POST', 'http://example.com', 
    'name=alice', '--pretty=all', '--style=auto'], capture_output=True)
def show(b):
    res = []
    for c in b:
        if c == 0x1b: res.append('ESC')
        elif c < 32 and c != 10: res.append(f'[{c:02x}]')
        elif c == 10: res.append('[NL]')
        else: res.append(chr(c))
    return ''.join(res)
print(show(orig_r.stdout))
"

                f"error sending request for url ({current_url})\\n\\nCaused by:\\n    0: client error (Connect)\\n    1: tcp connect error\\n    2: {e}"

            # Format error message to match xh's format

            import errno as errno_mod
            if hasattr(e, 'errno') and e.errno is not None:

import subprocess, re

def normalize(b):
    b = re.sub(b'Elapsed time: [0-9.]+s', b'Elapsed time: Xs', b)
    b = re.sub(b'Date: [^\n]+\n', b'', b)
    return b

def normalize_boundary(b):
    b = re.sub(rb'boundary=[a-f0-9-]+', b'boundary=BOUNDARY', b)
    b = re.sub(rb'--[a-f0-9-]{63,}', b'--BOUNDARY', b)
    return b

def test(args, do_norm_boundary=False, label=None):
    my_r = subprocess.run(['/tmp/test-build2/executable'] + args, capture_output=True)
    orig_r = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable'] + args, capture_output=True)
    
    my_out = normalize(my_r.stdout)
    orig_out = normalize(orig_r.stdout)
    my_err = normalize(my_r.stderr)
    orig_err = normalize(orig_r.stderr)
    
    if do_norm_boundary:
        my_out = normalize_boundary(my_out)
        orig_out = normalize_boundary(orig_out)
    
    ok = (my_out == orig_out and my_err == orig_err and my_r.returncode == orig_r.returncode)
    name = label or ' '.join(args[:4])
    if ok:
        print(f'MATCH: {name}')
    else:
        print(f'DIFFER: {name}')
        if my_r.returncode != orig_r.returncode:
            print(f'  exit: {my_r.returncode} vs {orig_r.returncode}')
        if my_err != orig_err:
            print(f'  stderr mine: {repr(my_err[:100])}')
            print(f'  stderr orig: {repr(orig_err[:100])}')
        if my_out != orig_out:
            for i in range(min(len(my_out), len(orig_out))):

# Error handling

BIGTEST

def normalize(b):
    b = re.sub(b'Elapsed time: [0-9.]+s', b'Elapsed time: Xs', b)
    b = re.sub(b'Date: [^\n]+\n', b'', b)
    return b

def normalize_boundary(b):
    b = re.sub(rb'boundary=[a-f0-9-]+', b'boundary=BOUNDARY', b)
    b = re.sub(rb'--[a-f0-9-]{63,}', b'--BOUNDARY', b)
    return b

# But the "Inferred port" warning comes AFTER that blank line in mine
# In original: both warnings, then blank line at end

# But the Inferred port warning is added INSIDE build_curl_cmd or in main() which is AFTER the blank line

# And the blank line should only be added after ALL warnings

        if ns.print_format:
            sys.stderr.write("Warning: Ignored -p/--print\\n")
            _curl_warned = True
        if _curl_warned:
            sys.stderr.write("\\n")  # blank line after warnings'''

        sys.stdout.write(cmd + '\\n')

content = content.replace(old2, new2, 1)

    b = re.sub(b'Elapsed time: [0-9.]+s', b'Elapsed time: Xs', b)
    b = re.sub(b'Date: [^\n]+\n', b'', b)
    return b

def normalize_boundary(b):
    b = re.sub(rb'boundary=[a-f0-9-]+', b'boundary=BOUNDARY', b)
    b = re.sub(rb'--[a-f0-9-]{63,}', b'--BOUNDARY', b)
    return b

def test(args, do_norm_boundary=False, label=None):
    my_r = subprocess.run(['/tmp/test-build2/executable'] + args, capture_output=True)
    orig_r = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable'] + args, capture_output=True)
    
    my_out = normalize(my_r.stdout)
    orig_out = normalize(orig_r.stdout)
    my_err = normalize(my_r.stderr)
    orig_err = normalize(orig_r.stderr)
    
    if do_norm_boundary:
        my_out = normalize_boundary(my_out)
        orig_out = normalize_boundary(orig_out)
    
    ok = (my_out == orig_out and my_err == orig_err and my_r.returncode == orig_r.returncode)
    name = label or ' '.join(args[:4])
    if ok:
        print(f'MATCH: {name}')
    else:
        print(f'DIFFER: {name}')
        if my_r.returncode != orig_r.returncode:
            print(f'  exit: {my_r.returncode} vs {orig_r.returncode}')

# The raw string has \\\\S+ which means \\S+ in the actual string which means \S+ in regex
# Wait: r'^\\.TH XH 1 \\S+ \\S+' 
# In a raw string: \\ = literal backslash, \S = backslash S
# So the pattern is: ^\\.TH XH 1 \\S+ \\S+ 
# In the regex engine: \.TH XH 1 \S+ \S+ (match \S = whitespace class \S = not whitespace)
# Wait: \\S in a raw string = \S in regex = non-whitespace character class

# Actually: r'^\\.TH XH 1 \\S+ \\S+'
# = raw string, so no special escaping of backslash
# = the string contains: ^\\.TH XH 1 \\S+ \\S+
# = as regex: ^ \\.TH XH 1 \\S+ \\S+
# = ^ + literal backslash + . + TH XH 1 + non-whitespace+ + space + non-whitespace+
